rulingRelevantObservations: `txgio_parcel` IS on the allowlist, and the retirement's own authority is the published parcel index. This makes a token-substitution fix look available but it is NOT honest: the slot concerned is provenance.parcelSource, whose value on every kept payload names the source that SUPPLIED a parcel record; a retired account-keyed node has no parcel record, so naming one fabricates a source. Additionally the serve mirrors the zoning rail onto provenance.zoningSource regardless of what the payload sets (including when the payload sets nothing), so only a token the payload itself supplies in parcelSource/landUseSource would ever be read.

A facts-free retirement cannot pass S13 as written; therefore 'retire it with the current run id and no facts' (A-146 option B) is necessary but NOT sufficient for the walk to go green. The dispatch's premise that the stamp is the only thing between the excluded nodes and a green walk is the part that is wrong.

The two candidate rule fixes are the walk's own doctrine for retired rows, not new tolerance: the walk already grades a well-formed retirement as its own class (RECORD_RETIRED), excludes retired rows from servedCount (verify-walk.mjs:1409-1424), and gradeS13 already emits UNMEASURED when it has no token to judge.

The last GREEN staging walk (91c3bfd5, 2026-09-14T03:36:42Z, retiredCount 16) was green because its retired nodes still carried the old fact-shaped payload with an allowlisted parcelSource -- the very condition this ruling removes. Its retired block is not in the later 86-parcel sweeps.
